name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Pelagic Scout Drone — 'The Remora'
product_name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Pelagic Scout Drone — 'The Remora'
description:
The Remora is a semi-autonomous underwater reconnaissance drone developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric, designed for operation in GLMZ's submerged infrastructure — the flooded lower transit levels, the polluted harbor channels, the cistern networks beneath the city's industrial sectors. Its hull is modeled on pelagic fish morphology, using a flexible myomer-composite spine and undulating fin drives rather than propellers, which produces almost no acoustic signature and leaves no propeller wash. The Remora moves through water the way an organism does — sinuous, unhurried, and very difficult to detect.

Zheng-Dao's biological engineering background is visible throughout the drone's design. Its sensor suite mimics the lateral line system of fish — a distributed array of pressure-sensitive nodes along its hull that detect water displacement, vibration, and chemical gradients. This allows the Remora to navigate in zero-visibility water, detect the movement of personnel or vehicles at range, and track chemical plumes to their source. The drone's outer skin is coated in a biofilm layer that absorbs sonar pings rather than reflecting them, making it functionally invisible to standard underwater detection systems. Onboard processing handles autonomous navigation, but the drone can accept real-time operator commands through a low-frequency acoustic tether.

The Remora is used by salvage operators, intelligence contractors, infrastructure saboteurs, and anyone with operational interest in GLMZ's submerged spaces. The city's flooded lower levels are largely unmapped and unmonitored — a fact that makes the Remora both practically useful and philosophically significant. In a city where every surface is watched, the water beneath it remains dark.

specifications.endurance: 72 hours autonomous, unlimited on tether power feed
specifications.payload: Optional 2kg hardpoint (demolition charge, sample collector, or relay node)
specifications.acoustic_signature: Below ambient noise floor at all operational speeds

tactical_use: Operators deploy the Remora ahead of aquatic insertion teams to map routes, detect patrols or automated defenses, and identify structural access points. In sabotage operations, the payload hardpoint carries a shaped demolition charge that the drone places autonomously on designated targets — pipeline joints, cooling intake structures, submerged power conduits. Intelligence contractors use the chemical gradient tracking to sample water sources for biological agents, industrial effluents, or pharmaceutical compounds being disposed of illegally. The drone can also function as a relay node anchor, dropping a communications repeater in a flooded shaft to extend signal range for surface operators.
cultural_context: GLMZ's flooded undercity is a contested space with no official governance. The people who live and work there — salvagers, pipe gangs, infrastructure squatters — have their own codes and a deep suspicion of anything entering the water from above. A spotted Remora is treated as a surveillance incursion, and several pipe gang territories have standing bounties on recovered units. Zheng-Dao officially sells the Remora for 'infrastructure inspection and environmental monitoring,' a classification that satisfies the letter of licensing requirements while leaving the door open for every other application.
story_hooks: A Remora has been found drifting in a sealed cistern that shouldn't have any access points — someone navigated it in through a route that doesn't appear on any city map.
A salvager recovered a Remora with a full sensor log intact. The log shows something moving through the flooded transit tunnels that doesn't match any known vehicle or organism profile.
Zheng-Dao's environmental monitoring contract is a cover for systematic chemical sampling — someone is building a database of what corporations are dumping in the water and why.
The players need to cross a half-kilometer of flooded tunnel guarded by automated sonar mines. The only way through is to follow a Remora that knows the gaps.
